claims.text: High-temperature treatment of an Hf-coated zirconium-containing substrate can cause Zr to diffuse into the Hf and form an HfZr transition layer.
Room-temperature PVD followed by an optimized heat treatment will produce a uniform HfZr interdiffusion layer on zirconium-alloy fuel cladding.
The resulting HfZr interdiffusion layer will be ductile.
The HfZr interdiffusion layer will act as a barrier to oxygen ingress.
The HfZr interdiffusion layer has lower oxygen diffusivity than the relevant uncoated or conventionally coated baseline.
Formation of the HfZr transition layer enhances adhesion between the Hf coating and substrate.
Lower oxygen diffusivity and enhanced adhesion will slow oxidation kinetics relative to uncoated cladding.
An Hf interlayer will significantly reduce oxidation weight gain relative to uncoated or conventionally coated zirconium-alloy cladding.
An Hf interlayer will produce a thinner oxide scale relative to uncoated or conventionally coated cladding.
The oxide scale formed on Hf-coated cladding will be more adherent than that formed on the baseline cladding.
Hf-coated cladding will retain appropriate mechanical properties for reactor service.
The proposed coating will maintain cladding mechanical integrity during or after high-temperature oxidation.
Air exposure at 1600 °C for 5 hours is representative of accident-scenario oxidation conditions for zirconium-alloy fuel cladding.
Performance critically depends on obtaining a uniform Hf layer.
Performance critically depends on precise control of Hf-Zr interdiffusion kinetics.
